candidates.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
candidates.abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出智能体式操作策略AMP：由通用AI模型直接控制机械臂并按任务进展调整动作；AMP1在单臂、双臂和移动操作中零样本取得SOTA，优于VLA和WAM基线。

candidates.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
candidates.title_zh: 计算机使用代理是具身通才
candidates.abstract: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. These results suggest that the skills CUAs learn on software, such as visual grounding, precise clicking, and exploration, already carry over to embodied tasks, giving CUAs a far broader scope in embodied AI than previously realized. We therefore advocate that computer-use agents can be embodied generalists. Further, we advocate that, by following the training strategy that made computer-use agents general, embodied AI can converge on a single general model as well, ushering in a new era of general embodied AI. Website: https://pranjal2041.github.io/cua-embodied
candidates.summary_zh: 提出将具身任务表述为与数字软件的交互：屏幕渲染物理环境视图并提供控制，通用计算机使用代理通过截图和键鼠操作完成具身任务。
candidates.contribution_zh: 单一CUA设计无需竞赛专属调优，在四个ECCV工作坊竞赛获第一、二、三、六名，表明软件技能可迁移至具身任务。

candidates.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
candidates.title_zh: SURE：面向高效视觉-语言-动作学习的时空不确定性表示
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have become a promising paradigm for end-to-end robot control, but their effectiveness still depends heavily on large volumes of demonstration data. In manipulation tasks, this dependence is compounded by structured spatiotemporal uncertainty in the action space: multiple nearby actions or trajectories may successfully solve the same task, while semantically equivalent demonstrations often unfold at different speeds. Standard pointwise supervision treats each demonstrated action as an exact target, imposing an unnecessary learning burden under such uncertainty. We present SURE, a data-efficient VLA training framework that explicitly models both spatial and temporal uncertainty. SURE augments a VLA backbone with a lightweight transposed-convolutional probabilistic action decoder that captures spatial uncertainty through local correlations among neighboring action bins. It further introduces Soft-DTW alignment supervision to accommodate local timing variations between predicted and demonstrated action chunks. Together, these two components reduce sensitivity to demonstrator-specific poses and execution timing, enabling more data-efficient action learning. We evaluate SURE on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world manipulation tasks. Even with only 10% of the demonstration data or 20% of the training steps, SURE achieves manipulation success rates that match or surpass baseline VLAs.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出数据高效的VLA训练框架，用转置卷积概率动作解码器建模空间不确定性，并以Soft-DTW对齐监督容忍执行时序差异；在LIBERO、RoboTwin 2.0和真实操作任务上，仅用10%示范数据或20%训练步数即达到或超越基线。
candidates.contribution_zh: 显式建模动作空间的空间与时序不确定性，降低对示范姿态和速度的敏感度，显著提升VLA数据与训练效率。

candidates.title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
candidates.title_zh: ODEAction：从预测动作块到演化动作
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, organizing continuous robot execution into separately predicted segments and thus introducing potential discontinuities at action-chunk transitions. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action-chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. Given visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioceptive information, ODEAction learns an action transition field defined over action space, where a transition vector characterizes the evolution rate of the current action with respect to evolution time. During execution, the model takes the current action as its initial condition and integrates the learned field using an ordinary differential equation (ODE), recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as an action head and does not depend on a specific vision-language backbone architecture. Experiments on LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin, and real robots show that ODEAction improves both task performance and trajectory quality over matched action-chunking baselines, with particularly pronounced gains on fine manipulation tasks.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出无动作块的VLA动作生成范式，学习动作空间转移场并用ODE积分递归生成连续动作，可作通用动作头，在仿真与真实机器人任务中提升性能与轨迹质量。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将动作块预测替换为连续动作演化，学习动作转移场并以ODE积分生成动作，缓解动作块衔接不连续问题。

candidates.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
candidates.title_zh: 在具有测试时基于模型强化学习的世界模型中编码记忆
candidates.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories. However, despite this progress, current approaches still struggle to surpass human performance on tasks that require long-term memory and planning. In this work, we address the problem of long-term memory in MBRL by moving beyond the commonly studied paradigm of architecture design. We introduce Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), using gradient descent at test time to encode the memory of episode observations into world model parameters. This enables the agent to learn a distinct world model for each episode, improving memory capabilities compared to traditional approaches that solely rely on contextual memory. We first establish a proof of concept on a simplified two-dimensional variant of the Memory Maze environment, which we refer to as Memory Maze 2D, showing consistent improvements across different world model architectures. We then demonstrate the effectiveness of TT-MBRL in the 3D domain, achieving new state-of-the-art results on the Memory Maze benchmark. Finally, we show that TT-MBRL maintains strong performance on non-memory benchmarks such as DeepMind Control and Atari 100k.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出TT-MBRL，在测试时用梯度下降将单回合观测记忆编码进世界模型参数，为每回合学习专用世界模型，提升长时记忆与规划，在Memory Maze达SOTA并保持DMC/Atari性能。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将测试时梯度更新用于世界模型参数以存储回合记忆，系统验证跨架构与2D/3D环境，并在记忆迷宫基准取得新SOTA。

candidates.title: HiMEM: Hippocampus-Inspired Memory Consolidation, Pruning, and Composition for Vision-Language-Action Models in 3D Scenes
candidates.title_zh: HiMEM：受海马体启发的3D场景视觉-语言-动作模型记忆巩固、剪枝与组合
candidates.abstract: Memory plays a crucial role in long-horizon task execution and cross-task generalization for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models operating in complex 3D scenes. However, existing VLA memory mechanisms suffer from memory noise, particularly in complex 3D scenes, as stored episodic memories contain extensive redundant details about scene layouts, object configurations, and robot-specific states, which obscure generalizable manipulation principles and hinder cross-task transfer. To address this challenge, we first introduce a hippocampus-inspired memory consolidation mechanism that synthesizes extensive episodic experiences into a compact set of essential semantic memories, enabling VLA models to derive generalizable principles from practical experience. Second, we propose an episodic memory pruning mechanism that removes redundant episodic memories whose contents are captured by consolidated semantic memories, thereby increasing effective memory capacity and improving long-horizon task execution. Finally, to handle complex task scenarios, we develop a flexible memory composition mechanism that jointly leverages multiple episodic and semantic memories to enhance cross-scenario generalization. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus demonstrate the effectiveness of HiMEM across different VLA backbones, improving the average success rate of pi_0 from 91.88% to 98.20% on LIBERO.
candidates.summary_zh: 针对VLA在复杂3D场景中的记忆噪声，提出海马体启发的语义记忆巩固、情景记忆剪枝与灵活记忆组合机制，提升长程任务执行和跨任务泛化，并在LIBERO系列上验证有效。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出面向VLA的海马体启发记忆巩固、冗余情景记忆剪枝和多记忆组合框架，减少记忆噪声并提升长程操作成功率。

candidates.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning
candidates.title_zh: MDF++：端到端表征学习的视触觉世界动作模型
candidates.abstract: Recently, world-action models (WAMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for robot manipulation. By jointly modeling action generation and future observation prediction, WAMs can act and anticipate the outcomes of the actions. However, existing WAMs typically rely on frozen pretrained encoders trained with reconstruction, which may not produce representations well suited for robot control. In this paper, we tackle the problem of learning physicallygrounded, control-relevant representations for WAMs. We propose MDF++, a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns latent representations of multisensory observations end-to-end with a diffusion backbone. While naive joint training can lead to feature collapse, MDF++ introduces a multi-task learning strategy that leverages cross-modal correlations to learn task-relevant representations. We evaluate MDF++ on a suite of contact-rich manipulation tasks, including realworld bolt screwing and nut mating, and show that it outperforms WAMs built on frozen pretrained representations by up to 50%. Additional videos are available on our website: jointmdf.github.io.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出MDF++，将多感官观测的潜在表征与扩散骨干端到端联合学习，用多任务策略利用跨模态相关性避免特征坍缩，在接触密集型操作任务上超越冻结预训练编码器的WAM最多50%。
candidates.contribution_zh: 端到端学习视触觉世界动作模型的潜在表征，提出多任务学习策略利用跨模态相关性防止特征坍缩，并在真实接触密集操作中验证。

candidates.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
candidates.title_zh: 迈向智能体化具身智能时代
candidates.abstract: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出A2-MEAS具身多智能体框架，以代码为扩展接口，用纠正码整合语言、空间证据与执行历史，并结合带潜世界模型的VLA策略A2-WLA，在BEHAVIOR、RoboTwin及真实机器人任务上取得显著提升。
candidates.contribution_zh: 构建以纠正码为接口的具身多智能体系统，A2-WLA在VLA中加入运动感知历史与潜世界模型，实现高效训练与长程失败恢复。

ai_review.reason: 提出具身多智能体框架与视觉语言动作模型，融合潜世界模型与失败恢复，属具身智能核心范围。
